2026-05-25 (v22): forge_overnight_drift_qqq KILLED before deployment. Strategy agent's #1 candidate from docs/AUDIT_2026_05_25_PART2/STRATEGY.md (~750 trades/year, the proposed biggest trade-volume multiplier). Built helio/overnight_drift.py + ops/audit/run_overnight_drift_backtest.py to gate-test before shipping a runner. 20y backtest on SPY/QQQ/IWM 2005-2026 FAILS at every plausible slippage: PF 0.72-0.81 @ 10bps (default), 0.90-0.97 @ 5bps (Strategy agent's stated assumption), 1.02-1.09 @ 2bps (institutional-tight, sub-retail-realistic). Even the best leg (QQQ @ 2bps) has CI lower 1.01 — still below the 1.20 floor. Walk-forward H1/H2 split both fail at every slippage. With 60-day Sharpe regime gate: marginally WORSE (gate strips ~30% of trades but kept ones still lose on average — slippage is the problem, not regime). Allocation entered at 0.0 + added to helio/roi_filter.KILLED_STRATEGY_CUTOFFS so any future attempt to launch a runner gets refused at the submit_bracket runtime invariant. Why it fails: overnight premium IS real (~5-7%/yr gross per Kelly-Clark 2011 / Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019) but daily-rotation pays 25%/yr in round-trip slippage at 10bps — the premium is a structural buy-and-hold harvest, not a tradeable signal. Code retained as research artifact — engine reusable for weekly-cadence variant (52 trades/year vs 250, drag drops 5x) or conditional-entry filter (only when ex-ante predicted move > cost). Lesson for future agent briefs: for any daily-frequency strategy, drag gross-edge by N×slippage before assuming it survives. Sprint 1 redirected to Variant Consensus Sleeve (Creative #2).
